title: House band at Chicago's Savoy Ballroom and a failed Tulsa booking
summary: Bernie Young's band was Savoy house band for about a year until Music Corporation of America booked it to Tulsa for a contract that fell through.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah, the whole band. Then we were the house band for the Savoy Ballroom.
The Savoy Ballroom -- we were there at the Savoy for about a year.
On King's Drive -- on South Parkway --
(unintelligible) King's Drive. Not too far from the theater -- from the --
And what were you -- the house band at the Regal -- you played all the shows -- the stage shows?
No, no. We were the house band at the Savoy.

At the Savoy. No, we played -- yes, we played all the dances, we played for all the engagements that they would have there. And how we got out from there, we had booked -- how did Bernie Young get out of that contract? It took him about a whole day to get out of that, but I don't know. Music Cooperation of America booked him down to Tulsa, Oklahoma, and he supposed to have a contract about ten, 15 years with them. And it wasn't so, so until after we got down there. We played one dance pavillion down there and we played the dance pavillion and we came back here to Chicago and wasn't nothing else to play. That's when I started arranging and gigging. I arranged for Earl Hines.
